newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees lower world 96/97 sugar output, surplus.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees lower world 96/97 sugar output, surplus.

text.p: World sugar production should reach 123.34 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, down from the 123.90 million reported for 1995/96, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Friday.
The ISO forecast a world sugar surplus of 2.80 million tonnes for 1996/97, which was sharply lower than the 1995/96 figure of 5.94 million tonnes.
World sugar consumption was estimated at 120.54 million tonnes after 117.96 million a year earlier.
The ISO said the projected 1996/97 surplus should not be regarded in isolation as the 1995/96 crop year also saw a surplus.

"It must be borne in mind that a surplus of 5.9 million tonnes resulted from the 1995/96 crop cycle and therefore the combined surplus over the two crop cycles is a substantial 8.7 million tonnes," it said.
"Even if a high proportion of the surplus is locked up in India, there is no doubt that the world sugar economy suffers from a large stock overhang, not seen since 1991/92."
